chunks: He said: Muhammad ibn Bashr narrated to me, saying: Hasan ibn Sama'a narrated to me, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
I and the Qaim (the Awaited Imam) are not from the same father.

key_terms.أَبٌ: Father, referring to lineage or paternity
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim, a title for the Awaited Imam (Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'I and the Qaim are not from the same father' mean regarding the identity of the Qaim?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies the lineage of the Qaim to refute the Waqifiyya, who erroneously claimed that Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) was the final Imam who would not die. By stating 'He and the Qaim are not from the same father,' the Imam distinguishes the Qaim as a distinct individual from Musa al-Kadhim, thereby preserving the doctrine of the eventual reappearance of the Mahdi while correcting the specific genealogical misunderstanding of the sect.
